clinician.final_diagnosis: severe COVID-19 pneumonia complicated by multiorgan thrombosis including myocardial ischaemia, left ventricular thrombus, intracranial thrombosis and mesenteric involvement despite prophylactic anticoagulation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old man, 7 days post-SARS-CoV-2 positive, presented with central compressive chest pain, shortness of breath, and other COVID-19 symptoms. Initial assessment revealed hypoxemia (SpO2 92% on RA), sinus tachycardia (113 bpm), and sparse fine-end inspiratory crepitations. ECG showed right heart strain with new-onset right bundle branch block. Laboratory tests revealed grossly elevated D-dimer (5483 ng/mL) and highly raised troponins (504 ng/L, uptrending to 1645 ng/L). Chest X-ray showed diffuse patchy airspace shadowing consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia. A bedside transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) revealed a globular dilated left ventricle with an ejection fraction of 35% and regional wall motion abnormalities (akinetic apical, anteroseptal, and anterior walls). A subsequent contrast echocardiogram confirmed a large pedunculated left ventricular thrombus.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms consistent with COVID-19 and cardiac involvement.
Initial physical exam showed hypoxemia and respiratory findings consistent with pneumonia.
ECG showed right heart strain and new-onset right bundle branch block, indicating cardiac stress/injury.
Elevated D-dimer and troponins indicated a hypercoagulable state and myocardial injury.
Chest X-ray confirmed severe COVID-19 pneumonia.
Echocardiogram revealed severe left ventricular dysfunction (EF 35%) with regional wall motion abnormalities, consistent with myocardial ischemia.
A large pedunculated left ventricular thrombus was confirmed by contrast echocardiogram.
